evidence.title: Covid, Brexit and Liz Truss mini-budget led to lasting decline in mental health, study finds

occurrences.checkable_against: UCL study analysis of GHQ-12 scores and UK GP depression attendance data
occurrences.quote_span: Their analysis of the general health questionnaire’s GHQ-12 screening tool, which measures mental health, found that the UK’s vote to leave the European Union led to an increase in overall mental ill-health equivalent to about 120,000 more people overall seeking a GP’s help for depression.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: UK population mental health impact of systemic shocks

occurrences.checkable_against: Published UCL study and Annie Jeffery's statement
occurrences.quote_span: “The past decade or so has been tumultuous, shaped by multiple overlapping shocks and ongoing uncertainty and instability that have impacted mental health in Britain,” said Jeffery.

occurrences.subject: UK population mental health impact of systemic shocks

occurrences.checkable_against: UK Household Longitudinal Study dataset and the UCL study methods
occurrences.quote_span: Researchers led by Dr Annie Jeffery of University College London used data from the UK Household Longitudinal Study of 87,857 people aged 16 and older, which was collected every year between 2009 and 2024, to estimate the mental health impact of those five “systemic shocks”.

occurrences.subject: UK population mental health impact of systemic shocks

occurrences.checkable_against: Published UCL study in BMJ Mental Health

occurrences.checkable_against: Published UCL study of UK mental health trends
occurrences.quote_span: Brexit, Liz Truss’s mini-budget and other “shocks” over the last 10 years have led to a serious and lasting deterioration in the UK population’s mental health, research has found.

occurrences.checkable_against: Centre for Mental Health research on the annual economic cost of mental ill-health

occurrences.checkable_against: Mind statement and NHS mental-health demand and capacity statistics
occurrences.quote_span: The huge rise in demand for care – driven by “shocks” causing anxiety, stress and worry – has left NHS services struggling “as more people than ever are reaching out for support”, said Tom Pollard, the mental health charity Mind’s director of policy, campaigns and public affairs.
occurrences.speaker: Tom Pollard
occurrences.subject: UK population mental health impact of systemic shocks

occurrences.checkable_against: NHS England mental health services contact statistics
occurrences.quote_span: The total number of people in England in contact with NHS mental health services almost doubled from 2.64 million in 2016-17 to 4.13 million in 2024-25.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: UK population mental health impact of systemic shocks

occurrences.checkable_against: Published UCL study results
occurrences.quote_span: All five events caused immediate and serious damage to overall mental wellbeing across the UK. But the Brexit referendum in June 2016 and first pandemic lockdown in March 2020 caused the most damage, the research team found.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: UK population mental health impact of systemic shocks

occurrences.checkable_against: Published UCL study results
occurrences.quote_span: “We observed increased psychological distress immediately after the Brexit referendum and the first Covid-19 lockdown, with more insidious monthly increases in psychological distress after the Russian invasion of Ukraine and the 2022 mini-budget,” said Jeffrey.
occurrences.speaker: Annie Jeffery
occurrences.subject: UK population mental health impact of systemic shocks

occurrences.checkable_against: UCL study analysis of monthly GHQ-12 scores and GP depression attendance
occurrences.quote_span: Russia’s offensive against Ukraine in February 2022 led to about 15,000 more Britons a month seeking a GP’s help for depression.

occurrences.subject: UK population mental health impact of systemic shocks

occurrences.checkable_against: BMJ Mental Health publication record
occurrences.quote_span: The UCL-led team’s findings have been published in the journal BMJ Mental Health.

occurrences.subject: UK population mental health impact of systemic shocks

occurrences.checkable_against: Published UCL study trend analysis
occurrences.quote_span: They found that psychological distress had been increasing in the UK from 2009 to a degree that was clinically significant but accelerated from 2015 onwards.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: UK population mental health impact of systemic shocks

occurrences.checkable_against: UCL study analysis of psychological distress and GHQ-12 scores
occurrences.quote_span: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the first and second Covid lockdowns also triggered big rises in psychological distress, as measured by the number of people with depression and anxiety.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: UK population mental health impact of systemic shocks

occurrences.checkable_against: Published UCL study results
occurrences.quote_span: All five events caused immediate and serious damage to overall mental wellbeing across the UK.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: UK population mental health impact of systemic shocks

occurrences.checkable_against: Published UCL study follow-up analysis of UK psychological distress
occurrences.quote_span: Even though the most recent of the five events occurred in 2022, the heightened distress in the population that followed them has persisted and not gone back to the much lower levels seen before 2016, they found.

occurrences.subject: UK population mental health impact of systemic shocks
